title: How to create better sales collateral with AI
description: Turn CRM, meeting, email, and account context into personalized sales collateral—from one-pagers and slides to interactive pages.
introduction: Most sales collateral starts with a scavenger hunt. The useful context is spread across meeting notes, email, CRM, old decks, product material, and someone’s memory. By the time it becomes a one-pager or presentation, it is often generic, stale, or disconnected from the conversation it is meant to move forward.

Strawberry is a browser with built-in AI agents. Your companion can work with the context already available across your tabs, meetings, files, CRM, email, connected apps, and past work—then turn it into a customer-facing asset built for the decision in front of you. That asset might be a one-pager, slide deck, tailored page, interactive calculator, workflow visual, or something else entirely.

sections.title: Start with the decision, not the format

blocks.text: A useful sales asset has a job to do. It might help a champion explain the idea internally, align a buying group on a pilot, make a proposed workflow tangible, answer an executive’s questions, or help someone decide what happens next.

Begin with the audience, the state of the conversation, and the outcome you want. If those are already clear from the account context, your companion can get to work without making you fill in another brief.

items.context: Turn the context around a real account into a customer-facing asset for the next decision or step.

sections.title: Bring the real account context together

blocks.text: The strongest sales collateral reflects what the customer has actually said: their priorities, questions, language, constraints, stakeholders, and next step. Strawberry can connect that conversation with the rest of the account context across meetings, CRM, email, open tabs, files, research, product material, and memory.

That matters because the asset is rarely a standalone piece of content. It is part of an ongoing relationship. Your companion can carry the context from research into the meeting, from the meeting into the asset, and from the asset into follow-up without asking you to reconstruct the story each time.

items.context: Fill important gaps about the account, stakeholders, and current situation before shaping the asset.
Turn a recent conversation into the priorities, commitments, objections, and next steps the asset should reflect.

sections.title: Choose the simplest format that can do the job

blocks.text: The format should follow the moment. Your companion can recommend one when it matters, or follow the direction you already have.

rows: A concise overview, pilot outline, proposal summary, or recap that should be easy to share
A narrative you will present, discuss with a group, or build toward a decision
A self-guided experience that brings the story, proof, and next step together
A situation where the customer should explore inputs, tradeoffs, value, or a proposed way of working
A different form better suits the audience, channel, or decision

blocks.text: The goal is not to make the most impressive artifact. It is to make the next conversation or decision easier.

sections.title: Make it specific without making things up

blocks.text: Specificity comes from the account context, not from adding more adjectives. Use the customer’s own language where it is accurate, show how the proposed work connects to their priorities, and keep the story focused on one useful next step.

Before external material is polished, check the claims that could change what you are comfortable sharing. Customer outcomes, ROI, pricing, security, timelines, product capabilities, and commitments should come from approved sources or remain clearly marked for review.

items: Use evidence and examples that fit the audience and claim.
Separate what the customer said from what your team is proposing.
Flag only the missing decisions or assumptions that materially affect the asset.
Keep a clear next step visible.

sections.title: Build it with a companion that learns what good looks like

blocks.text: Strawberry can move from the account story into the visual or interactive result, then critique the complete asset for clarity, accuracy, hierarchy, and usefulness. Because the work happens with the surrounding context still available, feedback can be specific: what to emphasize, what feels off-brand, what the customer will care about, and what should be removed.

Spend a little more time on the first asset. Your companion can learn from the version you accept—your narrative, brand direction, preferred sources, claim rules, and review style—so the next one starts much further ahead. Share the accepted creation method as a team skill when others should reuse it, or share the full companion when the team needs the same customer context across several sales workflows.

sections.title: Carry the context into the next step

blocks.text: Review the finished asset, then decide whether to share it with teammates for feedback or reuse, deliver it to the customer, publish it, or record it in the CRM. These are separate choices; approval of the asset should not silently approve the next one.

items.context: Deliver the approved asset with a message and follow-up that fit the relationship.
Record the approved asset, customer response, and resulting next step without silently changing the pipeline.

blocks.text: Open the Create a Sales Asset skill with one real account and a decision you want to move forward. Strawberry can bring the context together, recommend a useful form, and build something your customer will actually want to use.
